summary.intent: Determine whether phase 71 (share-invite security and IPNS data-integrity API) needed further discussion, then plan it end-to-end via the GSD tooling, resolving several architectural decisions (ownership check design, grant merge semantics, CID equivocation guard, and a share-table column rename) that surfaced during planning.
summary.outcome: Phase 71 was fully planned (9 PLAN.md files across 4 waves) and validated by the plan-checker and decision-coverage gate, with D-01 corrected to use ipns_records ownership checks instead of vaults (the original assumption was falsified by code), and a new D-10 full 'descriptor'-to-'key' rename plus D-04 CHECK-constraint folding absorbed into the plan set; everything was committed to branch feat/share-invite-security-and-ipns-data-integrity-api.

repo: CipherBox shares are always children of a user's vault — dto.rootIpnsName (invite.service.ts:172, ShareDialog.tsx:216) is the selected child node's IPNS name, never the vault root, so the `vaults` table (one row per user, unique owner_id) cannot be used to verify share ownership.

The only server-side signal for child-node ownership is ipns_records.user_id, documented as a 'non-authoritative creator marker' (authority is the record's Ed25519 signature, not row ownership) — but it's the only usable defense-in-depth check once vaults is ruled out.

shares.readDescriptorRef/writeDescriptorRef (and share_invites.encryptedKey) are literally just ECIES-wrapped keys with no extra packed metadata — the entity comment claiming '+ metadata' is inaccurate; grant metadata (rootNodeId, rootGeneration, rootIpnsName) lives in separate columns.

root_generation is a pinned snapshot of a node's generation at grant-issuance time, not derivable from live IPFS/IPNS metadata; it's load-bearing for anti-rollback (client reopen-prompt in navigate.ts:136/client.ts:1124,5330; server ConflictException forward-only check in shares.service.ts:275-282) and seeds the phase-70.1 floor-store/high-water durable generation floor.

The security-critical control for share/invite writes is that only a sharer who actually holds a folder's keys can produce a valid writeDescriptorRef via resolveShareWriteDescriptor — the DB ownership check is defense-in-depth, not the real access boundary.

shares/share_invites schema was introduced in the Phase 66 cutover migration (a DROP+CREATE), so it's still greenfield/unreleased and can be edited in place rather than requiring a forward rename migration.

GSD's decision-coverage gate parser (decisions.cjs) only recognizes decisions written as `- **D-NN …**` bullets; CONTEXT.md written with `### D-NN — Title` headings parses as zero decisions (treated as category headings), causing a false 'passed: false' even when all decisions are actually covered.

ipns_records.ipnsName is globally @Unique, which is what makes the vault-root ownership signal trustworthy for the true spoofing threat (an attacker can't re-register another user's already-claimed vault root).

code.finding: rootIpnsName is set to the selected item's ipnsName (any child node), not the vault root — the fact that falsified D-01's original vaults-based ownership check.

Server enforces forward-only rootGeneration and seeds the recipient's durable generation floor from the grant's rootGeneration; regression throws ConflictException — core of the anti-rollback machinery hardened in phase 70.1.

workflow: When a discussion/decision log might already exist on a branch, check git branches/history before re-running a discuss-phase workflow — avoids redundant discussion work.
Rebase a feature branch onto latest main before kicking off phase planning so the plan is grounded on current code.
When a planner subagent flags a locked decision as broken by real code (grep-verified), independently verify the claim before escalating to the user — don't just relay the subagent's assertion.

Background subagents can switch the shared git checkout out from under the orchestrator (a subagent created a slug-named branch and HEAD followed) — always re-verify branch/HEAD state after an agent returns before proceeding.

For a scoped identifier rename with a large blast radius, split the decision into DB-column-only vs TypeScript-property/API-field rename — they have very different costs (single migration vs cross-stack refactor spanning TS, Rust, and codegen).
When a GSD gate fails, check whether it's a genuine block or a known parser/format false-negative before treating it as blocking (also matches existing memory: GSD commit_failed false-negative).
Resuming a still-alive planner subagent with new decision context (via SendMessage) is cheaper than re-spawning cold once it has already analyzed most of the phase's decisions.

friction: The plan-checker's decision-coverage gate returned a spurious 'passed: false' due to a CONTEXT.md heading-format mismatch, requiring source-diving into decisions.cjs to find the exact expected bullet syntax before it could be fixed.

The planner subagent's final report incorrectly warned about being on the 'wrong branch' (Phase 70.1 branch) when in fact a background subagent had already switched HEAD to the correct phase-71 slug branch — required manual reconciliation to confirm nothing was actually broken.
zsh glob mangling required falling back to `git grep` to get accurate rename blast-radius counts.

Locked decision D-01 from the phase-71 discussion branch turned out to rest on a false premise (rootIpnsName == vault root), discovered only during planning — required unwinding and re-deciding mid-plan, plus a second planner revision pass for D-10 (rename) and amended D-04.

71-05 (sdk-e2e live-stack concurrent first-publish race) and 71-02/71-01 are marked autonomous:false / manual — will need a human-run verification step during execution.
